Definition: emptiness or vanity; figuratively, something transitory and unsatisfactory; often used as an adverb
BiblicalUsage: Hebel means breath, vapour, vanity, and it is the word Ecclesiastes cannot stop saying. In Ecclesiastes 1:2 all is vanity, in Ecclesiastes 1:14 all is vanity and vexation of spirit, in Psalms 39:5 every man at his best state is altogether vanity, and in Job 7:16 Job says he would not live alway, for his days are vanity.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word is not despair but honesty: life without God is a breath that passes, and the Teacher says it so that I will stop building on breath. The answer is not to pretend the vapour is solid, but to fear God and keep his commandments.
